title: Deciphering Genetic Susceptibility of Pemphigus through Immunomics
text:
Pemphigus is an autoimmune blistering skin disease that occurs sporadically across the globe but is triggered
by still unknown environmental antigens in endemic areas. Although its etiology is poorly known, it has been
demonstrated that the variation of the extended major histocompatibility complex (MHC) is strongly associated
with a differential risk of developing pemphigus. Here, we will apply State-of-the-Art multi-omics approaches to
discover causal variants, reactive antigens, and disease mechanisms.

title: 3D Chromatin architectural dynamics at ultra-high resolution
text:
Dysregulation of gene expression is a major cause of disease. Because most elements that control gene
expression are located far distal to the genes they control, we must understand 3D genome folding to understand
gene regulation. Through the application of new cutting-edge methods, this proposal will gain new insights into
how 3D genome folding regulates gene expression.

title: Simultaneous profiling of neuronal synapse activities, proteins, and messenger RNAs at the single-cell level
text:
Neurodevelopmental diseases such as autism spectrum disorder have major health impacts in the US.
Understanding how complex polygenic variations associated with these diseases affects neuronal activity in
human patient populations is crucial to the identification of new therapeutics to treat these debilitating diseases.

title: Role of ALDH1A in endometrial homeostasis and endometriosis inflammation
text:
Endometrial stem cells, although not well understood, are largely implicated in endometriosis which is a
debilitating disease that affects 190 million individuals worldwide. This project aims to uncover the role of
endometrial stem cell marker ALDH1A in endometrial homeostasis and subsequently investigate ALDH1A’s role
in endometriosis inflammation using patient-derived endometriotic lesion organoids and genetically engineered
mouse models. Uncovering the role of ALDH1A in normal endometrial function as well as in endometriosis will
provide novel therapeutic targets to improve treatment outcomes for patients with endometriosis and other
reproductive diseases.

title: The role of T cells in tendon healing
text:
Tendon ruptures and tendinopathies are painful and debilitating conditions affecting a large portion of the
adult population. From a regenerative standpoint, there is a pressing clinical need to identify the cell and
molecular mechanisms regulating tendon differentiation vs fibrotic scarring in order to improve repair
outcomes. Since the local immune environment and T cells are implicated in both effective and poor
tendon healing, the objective of the proposed studies is to fully define the T cell subpopulations
underlying tendon healing and to test the role of IL33.

title: Investigating the molecular composition of the parasitophorous vacuole during Encephalitozoon intestinalis infection
text:
Encephalitozoon intestinalis is one of the most prevalent species of microsporidia found in humans and can
lead to fatal disease in immunocompromised individuals. While E. intestinalis causes significant disease
burden, our understanding of how these parasites develop within their host remains limited. Thus, using
cellular, proteomic, and structural approaches we will investigate the molecular and cellular features of the
replicative niche established during infection and uncover how these parasites successfully replicate within
their host, ultimately leading to the development of novel therapeutic strategies which are currently limited.

title: Multisensory learning to support accessible interactive tools for math
text:
The objective of this project is to deliver directly accessible interfaces for educational
math content for students who are blind or have low vision (BLV). The accessible
learning tools (ALT) that will be produced will have three different interfaces within the
same tool: a traditional drag-and-drop, and an audio-based system, and a multisensory
learning input that uses physical pieces and computer vision. The activities created for
the ALT system will be aligned to curricula that is currently in the market and have been
shown to be effective in teaching math concepts. Health impacts will be increased self-
efficacy and independence for BLV students in school, and persistence into STEM
careers and employment.

title: Development of an Efficient High Throughput Technique for the Identification of High-Impact Non-Coding Somatic Variants Across Multiple Tissue Types
text:
Somatic mutations (genomic variants that occur after conception) have long been known to be an important
cause of cancer, but recent research has found that they are also responsible for a range of other human
disorders as well as phenotypic variations between individuals. The overall goal of the Somatic Mosaicism
across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network is to gain a better understanding of how somatic mutations
influences biology and disease. As part of the SMaHT network, the goal of our project is to develop better and
cheaper methods of detecting somatic mutations that are likely to influence human biology.

title: Developing a Donor-Candidate Risk Prediction System to Optimize Lung Allocation and Transplant Outcomes
text:
The donor lung supply is inadequate to meet the ever-increasing need of patients awaiting transplant.
Compounding this problem, the US lung transplant system does not consider all known donor and patient
information available at time of an organ offer, missing the opportunity to maximize best use of organs and
survival gained from each transplant. This research will contribute to the development of a system that will use
all known data at the time of an organ offer to find the best donor and patient match improving utilization of
available organs and maximizing transplant patient survival.

title: Acquisition of a Confocal Microscope to Support Research, Teaching, and Technical Skill Development
text:
This project will acquire a FLUOVIEW FV4000 Confocal Laser Scanning Microscope to enhance neuroscience
and cell biology research at Chicago State University. The instrument will support interdisciplinary studies on
neurodegenerative diseases, the effects of forever chemicals, and the understanding of brain health and
behavior—areas of high public health importance. This project will advance CSU’s mission to strengthen
scientific training and foster collaboration across departments at an under-resourced university.

title: Roles of Macropinocytosis in HIV-1 infection of CD4+ T Cells
text:
Relevance:
Entry of a virus into host cells, which can occur at different subcellular locations, is the first and essential step
in virus infection. The goal of the proposed research is to determine how HIV-1, which causes AIDS, enters its
natural host CD4+ T cells and thus establishes productive infection. Knowledge obtained from the proposed
studies will help us develop novel antiviral strategies that may inhibit spread of this virus to uninfected host
cells.

title: Nanomaterials to improve growth factor delivery to the cornea
text:
Protein growth factors are integral to effective corneal wound healing, and numerous proteins have shown
promise as therapeutic agents; however, practical challenges associated with topical protein-based therapies
limit or prevent their clinical use. The proposed research aims to improve our methods of protein delivery to the
ocular surface through the development of a sustained drug-release, nanocomposite hydrogel. This novel
biomaterial will be developed using nerve growth factor as a model protein therapeutic, tested on in vitro and in
vivo models of diabetic keratopathy, and will result in a drug delivery system poised to be translated into clinical
applications.

title: Targeting MED31-driven transcription recycling in lethal prostate cancer
text:
The proposed studies will discover MED31-driven transcription recycling as a novel oncogenic mechanism
contributing to progression of lethal castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). Our studies will yield detailed
molecular insight into the control of aberrant transcription recycling in lethal prostate cancer, while performing
preclinical development of a CRISPR/Cas13d RNA targeting-based nanotherapy targeting MED31-mediated
transcription recycling in CRPC.

title: Input specific adaptations to glutamatergic strength and plasticity on PFC PV-INs following ethanol drinking
text:
Although both men and women are affected by alcohol use disorder (AUD), women often progress through
AUD disease milestones faster and experience more severe health consequences than men; however, little is
known about the synaptic and molecular mechanism driving these sex-differences. The sexually dimorphic
prefrontal cortex (PFC) integrates excitatory glutamatergic inputs from subcortical structures to modulate
cortical excitation, yet the mechanism by which ethanol alters these inputs remains unclear. This proposal
seeks to investigate how ethanol alters glutamatergic strength and plasticity at discrete excitatory inputs to the
PFC in female and male mice.

title: Modeling Hormone-Dependent Male Breast Cancer in Rats
text:
Current male breast cancer (MBC) research is severely constrained by the lack of physiologically relevant
preclinical models. Our innovative ACI rat model addresses this critical gap by providing the first
comprehensive platform specifically designed to investigate MBC pathogenesis and therapeutic responses.
Through this proposal, we will establish foundational knowledge of hormonal dependencies and create robust
in vitro and in vivo models, providing an unprecedented resource for the MBC research community.

title: Follistatin-like 1 Mediated Host Defense in Bacterial Pneumonia
text:
Bacterial pneumonia is a major health burden worldwide, and new treatment approaches are
urgently needed. Follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL-1) is a novel host immunomodulator in the
lung, though the role of FSTL-1 in lung host defense is unknown. This proposal aims to
determine the molecular and cellular requirements of FSTL-1-mediated pulmonary host defense
pathway, and outcomes of these studies will inform host-derived, immune targeting therapeutic
approaches for the treatment of bacterial pneumonia.

title: Characterization of schizophrenia liability genes in models of human microglial synaptic pruning
text:
Schizophrenia is a chronic, prevalent, and disabling mental disorder, and efforts to develop more effective
treatments are hindered by a lack of understanding of disease biology. The investigators have developed
cellular models of synaptic pruning in schizophrenia, and will use these validated models to understand the
effect of recently-identified risk genes on synaptic pruning by studying human microglia as well as neurons.
This research will yield a prioritized list of potential treatment targets, and more generally provide a deeper
understanding of the way genes may contribute to schizophrenia risk.

title: A trial of the Sense2Quit App for Smoking Cessation
text:
Cigarette smoking remains a major cause of preventable death among people with HIV (PWH), who smoke at
significantly higher rates than the general population and experience compounded health risks. This project will
evaluate a novel mobile health (mHealth) intervention, the Sense2Quit App, which uses wearable sensor
technology and real-time behavioral support to help PWH quit smoking. Findings from this research will inform
scalable, evidence-based strategies to reduce tobacco-related use and improve long-term health outcomes in
Americans.

title: Cell type-specific neurotensin signaling in methamphetamine use disorder
text:
Methamphetamine use disorder and relapse in abstinent individuals represent ongoing and serious public
health issues, but the neurophysiological adaptations that are responsible are not adequately understood.
These studies will combine electrophysiological, behavioral, and cell type-specific techniques in mice to
elucidate the role of the modulatory peptide neurotensin in alterations that promote and maintain drug self-
administration. The mechanistic understanding gleaned from these studies could help identify novel
therapeutic targets to treat methamphetamine addiction and prevent relapse.

title: Transcriptional and Epigenetic Control of Totipotency and Early Development by Zfp281
text:
RELEVANCE
This renewal R01 research project aligns with the NIGMS mission by advancing basic research in the
understanding of the transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms underlying totipotency and early
developmental processes in mammals (mice in this case). The insights gained from studying the role of Zfp281
in zygotic genome activation and early embryonic development are poised to contribute significantly to the
foundational knowledge required for future breakthroughs in disease diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.
